identity.name: Protectorate General to Pacify the North
identity.wikipedia: Protectorate General to Pacify the North

land.text: 'the former territory of the Xueyantuo', which thirteen Tiele and Uyghur tribes gave up on 9 January 647

predecessors.note: Xueyantuo ended in 646 (its dossier); the tribes were organised under the jimi system.

land.text: the Mongolian Plateau, which the protectorate 'controlled from 647 to 682'; Ilterish founded the Second Turkic Khaganate by revolt in 682

successors.note: The protectorate itself survives until 784 (infobox) as small seats at Yunzhong and Shouxiang in Inner Mongolia; the page gives them no area, so this dossier ends with the plateau.

capitals.name: Yanran (Anbei seat on the Mongolian steppe)
capitals.note: The page says the seat 'began at Yanran, moved to Hanhai, and then to Anbei' without giving sites for 647-682 or coordinates. The point (central Mongolia, near the Orkhon) is the researcher's reading, not a page's.

correction.text: the Mongolian Plateau from Lake Baikal in the north to the Gobi Desert in the south, the Greater Khingan in the east and the Altai Mountains in the west: the former Xueyantuo lands, read as Outer Mongolia north of the Gobi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Established by the Tang dynasty in 647 to pacify the former territory of the Xueyantuo' and 'controlled the Mongolian Plateau from 647 to 682'; the page gives the bounds (Baikal, Gobi, Greater Khingan, Altai) and no area. Outer Mongolia minus the Gobi (about 1.1 M km2) is the researcher's reading; the Cliopatria Tang shapes of 633-681 that draw this land as direct Tang territory are wrong (see the Tang dossier).

region.text: the Mongolian Plateau from Lake Baikal in the north to the Gobi Desert in the south, the Greater Khingan in the east and the Altai Mountains in the west: the former Xueyantuo lands, read as Outer Mongolia north of the Gobi

ledger.note: 647: the Yanran Protectorate is established. 'On 9 January 647, thirteen Tiele and Uyghur tribes surrendered to the Tang' and the protectorate was 'established ... to pacify the former territory of the Xueyantuo'. The page dates the setting up of the Yanran Protectorate to 10 April 647, after the January surrender, so the found event is April 647 (reviewer ea-04-x).
663: the Yanran Protectorate becomes the Hanhai Protectorate ('On 5 February 663 the Yanran Protectorate' was renamed); in August 669 it becomes the Protectorate General to Pacify the North (Anbei).
669: the Hanhai Protectorate is renamed the Protectorate General to Pacify the North (Anbei) in August 669.

region.text: the Mongolian Plateau from Lake Baikal in the north to the Gobi Desert in the south, the Greater Khingan in the east and the Altai Mountains in the west: the former Xueyantuo lands, read as Outer Mongolia north of the Gobi

ledger.note: 682: the plateau is lost. The protectorate 'controlled the Mongolian Plateau from 647 to 682'; Ilterish Qaghan founded the Second Turkic Khaganate 'after a successful revolt in 682' (Western Turks page). The page itself describes no revolt.

wars.name: Revolt of Ilterish and the Second Turkic Khaganate

zones.text: the Mongolian Plateau from Lake Baikal in the north to the Gobi Desert in the south, the Greater Khingan in the east and the Altai Mountains in the west: the former Xueyantuo lands, read as Outer Mongolia north of the Gobi

wars.outcome: Ilterish Qaghan founded the Second Turkic Khaganate by revolt in 682 and the Tang lost the Mongolian Plateau.
wars.note: Only the 682 revolt is on the pages opened (Western Turks page); the Anbei page gives 682 as the end of its control of the plateau.

certainty.note: Steppe frontier, bounded only by Baikal, the Gobi, the Greater Khingan and the Altai on the page.

sources.note: 647 founding, the 663 and 669 renames, the bounds of the plateau, 682, the later seats to 784.

sources.title: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks
sources.note: Only for 'Ilterish Qaghan founded the Second Turkic Khaganate after a successful revolt in 682'.

notes: Written for ea-04-x on the Andong protectorate's pattern (type colony). The Tang dossier carries the same plateau as a vassal pair 647-682 with the counterpart string 'Tiele and Uyghur tribes (Yanran Protectorate)', and 646 gain from xueyantuo; this dossier is that unit. The infobox runs 647-784: after 682 the protectorate moved to Yunzhong (698), was revived at Shouxiang (714), renamed Zhenbei (757-784) and Anbei again in 843, but the page gives none of these an area, so they are not drawn (a gap-filler could add a Hetao rump from 698). The capital point is approximate and not from a page. Gazetteer: Outer Mongolia minus the Gobi is the researcher's reading of the page's bounds.
